Daily Briefing — Friday, May 8 2026

Enterprise agentic AI moves from experimentation to production governance, while financial services embrace AI-driven compliance automation

AI & Technology

#1 — Cognizant Launches Secure AI Services for Enterprise Agent Governance — AI Agent Store

★ Directly addresses Cristiano's core concern: enterprise governance and security frameworks for agentic systems at scale, transforming governance from optional oversight to a service line requirement.

Cognizant launched Secure AI Services to help enterprises secure, govern, and scale AI and agentic systems, covering secure agent development, AI behavior monitoring in production, identity and access management, agent behavior controls, evidence for audits, and generative AI risk management. This reflects buyers asking harder questions about accountability when agents take wrong actions.

#2 — Anthropic Doubles Claude Code Usage Limits and Expands Financial Services Agents — AI Agent Store & LLM News

★ Product capability expansion directly relevant to Claude-based workflows Cristiano is building; also signals Anthropic's push into financial services vertical with preconfigured agents.

Anthropic doubled Claude Code's five-hour usage limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans, and removed peak-hour reductions for Pro and Max. Anthropic released ten preconfigured AI agents for the financial sector designed to automate typical tasks performed by investment banks, asset managers and insurers.

#3 — Agentic AI Adoption Survey: 97% of Executives See Value, But Only 29% See ROI — WRITER & Deloitte

★ Critical data on the enterprise AI adoption gap—governance, organizational structure, and ROI measurement challenges that directly inform Eidosmedia's product strategy and Cristiano's CTO mandate.

79% of organizations face challenges in adopting AI—a double-digit increase from 2025—with 54% of C-suite executives admitting AI is tearing their company apart, despite 59% investing over $1 million annually in AI technology. Nearly all executives (97%) say their company deployed AI agents in the past year, with 52% of employees already using them.

Financial Services Technology

#1 — IMF Warns: Agentic AI Requires 'Know Your Agent' Frameworks for Financial Transactions — Biometric Update

★ Directly impacts R+ product and Eidosmedia's sell-side/buy-side clients; highlights regulatory shift toward agent identity verification in payments—governance risk for financial content operations.

Agentic AI is forcing a rethink of identity and authentication in payments, as systems designed for human approval struggle to handle transactions initiated by autonomous software. A new paper from the International Monetary Fund warns that AI agents capable of executing payments expose gaps in Know Your Customer (KYC) and multifactor authentication. The shift is driving demand for new frameworks that can verify both the identity of an AI agent and the user's delegated authority—effectively introducing 'Know Your Agent' models and continuous identity verification.
